title: G4: cor:auto only controls sign, not generator — endpoints in {3,4,7,8} not ruled out

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
In Corollary `cor:auto` (sec:enum), the Even-Enclosure Lemma gives that the two axis ends $(i,0),(j,0)$ of a region boundary component satisfy $j-i$ odd, hence (since the sign vector $\epsilon=(+,-,+,-,\dots)$ alternates) $\epsilon(i)\ne\epsilon(j)$. This gives only **opposite sign**, NOT $w_i=w_j^{-1}$. To conclude $w_i=w_j^{-1}$ one also needs $i,j$ to carry the **same generator**. Opposite sign alone is insufficient: e.g. position $1$ ($a$) and position $4$ ($b^{-1}$) have opposite sign but $w_1=a\ne b=w_4^{-1}$.

The proof handles this by the single sentence: "the only $A$-components with an end in $\{3,4,7,8\}$ are the fixed arcs themselves." This sub-claim is **load-bearing but unjustified**. One must rule out a region boundary component whose two axis ends are (a) one position in $P=\{1,2,5,6,9,10\}$ and one in $\{3,4,7,8\}$, or (b) two positions in $\{3,4,7,8\}$ from different short arcs (e.g. $4$ and $7$). In case (a)/(b) opposite-sign would NOT yield an inverse pair, breaking admissibility.

**Suggested fix.** Show $\{3,4\}$ and $\{7,8\}$ are innermost adjacent short arcs: the arc $\{3,4\}$ together with the axis segment $[3,4]\times0$ bounds a half-disk containing no arc-end (positions $3,4$ adjacent), so any region boundary component reaching position $3$ or $4$ stays on that short arc and joins $3$ to $4$; likewise $7,8$. Hence no region component links $\{3,4,7,8\}$ to the outside, and within $P$ every end carries generator $a$, so opposite sign $\Rightarrow$ inverse. This closes the gap.
